title: What If Mount Fuji Erupted Tomorrow?

scenes.text: What if Mount Fuji erupted? Ash, not lava, would be Tokyo's biggest problem.
Fuji last erupted in 1707, more than 300 years ago.
Japan's government models about 1.7 billion cubic meters of ash. Around 490 million would need hauling away.
Ash deeper than 3 centimeters can make wet roads impassable. Over 30 centimeters can collapse wooden houses.
Officials estimate up to 2.5 trillion yen in damage, about 16 billion dollars, and tell residents to stock two weeks of supplies.
Fuji is quiet today. But Japan now has a plan for the day it wakes.
